title: Make a button with states and properties, and set them on a copy
goal: Somebody who knows design tools sat down with components and could not do the one thing components are for. Take the whole journey and make it work end to end: draw a button, give it a label you can change per copy, give it a resting, hovered, pressed and disabled look, place copies, and set each copy's look and label without leaving the panel or guessing what anything is called.
notes:
Said by the user on 2026-09-15 as they walked away: "i can't use components at all it's totally confusing on how to create states and properties that I can choose at the instance level."

This task OWNS THE JOURNEY rather than a control. Its siblings each fix a part of it and should be done first or alongside:
- every-pane-says-what-it-is-for-in-words-somebody: renames Adjustable and Versions to what they actually are. The user could not name either.
- a-copy-of-a-component-is-configured-not-authored: makes a copy's panel show which version it shows and the values it can set, instead of the original's authoring wall.
- tutorials-making-states-in-a-component: teaches the same journey once it works.
If those land first this task may be mostly verification, and that is the right outcome. What it must never be is closed because its parts were closed: the point is that the whole thing works for somebody who has not read any of this.

EVERYTHING NEEDED ALREADY EXISTS in the model, which is why this is an IA and naming problem rather than a feature gap. Components hold versions, a copy picks which version it shows, versions can be named, originals define adjustable things, a copy can be given its own value, and several copies can be spoken for at once. All of that shipped between 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-13. The user is not asking for a feature; they are saying they cannot find the one that is there.

The four states are a CONVENTION on versions, not a feature: there is no hover or pressed or disabled anywhere in the model, checked. Name four versions after the four states. Do not invent a states feature to satisfy this task; make the versions mechanism findable and understandable instead, and if the convention turns out to need support the app does not have, file that rather than half building it here.

The measurement that matters is the first acceptance item. This whole complaint arrived because somebody competent tried it and could not. The task is not done because the controls exist; it is done when somebody can do it unaided.

THE MODEL, corrected by the user on 2026-09-15 while walking away. First: "I don't think 'Variants' is any better. component properties makes sense. Variant is a property of the component." Then, still thinking: "Maybe State is a separate property. or maybe variant is hierarchical."

So the direction is ONE concept, not two sections. A component has PROPERTIES. What the panel currently splits into 'Adjustable' and 'Versions' is one list: a property is anything a copy can be given its own answer for, and one KIND of property is a set of named looks, which is what Versions is today. That is why neither name worked: they are two names for halves of one idea.

This also collapses the copy's panel into the same list with values in it instead of definitions, which is what the sibling task a-copy-of-a-component-is-configured-not-authored is for.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and the user was explicitly unsure, so settle it with a prototype rather than a preference:
- Is a state just one property among many, named State with the values rest, hovered, pressed and disabled? That is the simplest answer and probably right.
- Or does a component need more than one look-changing property at once, so that a Button has a Type of primary or secondary AND a State of rest or hovered, and the two combine into a matrix of drawings? That is what the user means by variant being hierarchical, and it is what real button components need almost immediately.
The second is strictly more powerful and strictly more work, and the first is a special case of it. Prototype the matrix case before choosing, because designing for one look-changing property and discovering later that two are needed is a rewrite rather than an addition.

Do NOT settle this by picking a word. The question is whether the model holds one named-set property or several, and the naming falls out of the answer.
acceptance: The whole journey is walked by somebody who has not seen it, in one sitting, without being told anything, and every place they hesitate is written down
Making a thing adjustable per copy is findable and its name says what it is, so nobody has to open it to learn what it does
Making a second look for the same component is findable and its name says what it is
On a copy, choosing which look it shows is immediate and obvious: it is the main reason somebody selects a copy
On a copy, the adjustable things the original defined are right there with their values, editable, and nothing that only the original can do is shown
Four copies showing four different looks can be put side by side and told apart, and the audit captures that as the proof the journey works
The words used are the same in the panel, the menus, the canvas label and the tutorial, so nothing is called two things
Changing the original still updates every copy, and a copy given its own value keeps it, which is the behaviour that already exists and must not be lost
The audit states plainly whether somebody could now do this unaided, and if not, what is still in the way
Audit under queue/audits/ with the journey captured step by step, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: deps: the renames and the copy panel first; this verifies the whole journey works
user corrected the direction: states and properties are one list, and whether several look-changing properties combine is open

Measured, from rewriting the states tutorial: four states end up laid out by the app rather than by you, and the result does not read as a set. On the tutorial's own desk (canvas 720x480, button 240x52 at 88,88) adding Hover, Pressed and Disabled lands them at (352,88), (352,164) and (352,240): one drawing alone on the left with its copies underneath it, and three more in a column on the right. Nothing groups them, nothing says the four belong together, and there is no way to lay them out as a strip. Your acceptance item about four looks side by side is the fix; this is what it is up against today. Picture: queue/audits/2026-09-15-states-guide-page.png.

Also from the same pass: the only word the panel has for the set of looks is Variant, and the only way to make it say State is to type State over the property name yourself. The rewritten tutorial now teaches exactly that, because it is the only honest way to say state in the app's own words. Worth deciding here whether the journey should offer State as a starting point rather than leaving everybody to rename it.
